title: Transmission and Infection Prevention as well as Microbiological and Clinical Dynamics in Patients with Candidozyma auris Colonization (C. auris) and Infection (CauDy Study)
summary: Since June 2025, the yeast C. auris has been detected more frequently in patients at a university hospital, as well as in a collaborating external hospital. Severely ill patients, particularly those with ventricular assist devices (VADs), were especially affected. There is still limited knowledge about key issues such as risk factors for acquisition, how long colonization persists, how resistance develops, and the clinical course in these patients. We collect routine clinical data from patients known to be colonized with C. auris, thereby assessing the duration of colonization, risk factors, and clinical outcomes.
conditions: Colonization and infection with multidrug-resistant organisms

interventions.name: Prospectively, all patients with documented C. auris and ventricular assist devices (VADs) will be followed with regard to the occurrence of predefined endpoints.
